role_output.SUBSTANTIVE_LOC_ASSESSMENT: The six primary Python modules (model, store, policy, engine, runtime, cli) are roughly five thousand source lines before SQL/config/operator assets. Large sections are executable validation, branching, transactions, SQL state transitions, JetStream protocol handling, recovery and diagnostics. Thin continuityctl/starter_cli adapters, limited policy/engine override duplication, and a small unused repair affordance do not drive the scale; after discounting them, reachable substantive runtime/configuration remains comfortably above 3,000 LOC.
MAJOR_MODULES: model.py — shared domain identities/invariants for events, archive provenance, topology, effects/checkpoints, replay, leases and retention; imported throughout runtime/store/orchestration.
store.py + SQL — transactional durable authority for journal publication/acks, generations, archive, effects/quarantine/checkpoints, reconciliation, replay, leases and retention.
policy.py — inherited continuity orchestration for configuration/topology, generation validation, effects, reconciliation, replay/lease/retention, health and reports.

engine.py — reachable defect-bearing overrides for publication, generation observation, consumer dispatch/effect ordering, reconciliation, replay/fencing and retention; repairs must act on real durable/runtime interfaces.
runtime.py — real NATS/JetStream administration, physical publication acknowledgement, durable pulls, hub sourcing/archive sync and nats-server process lifecycle.
cli.py + starter_cli + continuityctl — external operator control plane wiring the task engine, store and real runtime; no separate verifier-only recovery path.
PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: Stable event identity crosses journal, NATS headers, replay and archive; fixing retry message-id alone does not fix premature durable publication/ack ordering, and vice versa.
Topology/source ownership and generation authority span config, model validation, durable origin generations and runtime bootstrap; a cosmetic stream fix is insufficient.

LeaseToken models exact epoch/owner/expiry, while replay performs pre/post-publish fencing and durable publish state changes; the starter's epoch/in-flight faults require coordinated lease issuance, fence validation and mutation ordering.

Replay-item terminal labels are progress metadata, not archive authority: execute_replay_plan rechecks durable archive membership, so later replay work cannot safely rely on stale completed-item state alone.

Consumer correctness spans real pull delivery, dispatch, deterministic effect records, quarantine, effect checkpoint, ack checkpoint and JetStream ack floor; ordering/idempotency cannot be repaired in one table.

Reconciliation/replay/retention share origin identity, archive provenance, required-consumer progress, active replay pins, holds, age and disconnect+replay+safety horizon; fixing only counts or only age leaves unsafe behavior.
role_output.REMOVAL_TEST: PASS. Removing approximately 25% cannot be confined to inert padding: runtime.py removes physical JetStream behavior; store/schema removes durable authority; model.py removes shared invariants; policy/engine removes recovery/reconciliation/consumer/retention orchestration; CLI wiring removes operator reachability. Thin adapters and inherited override duplication are far below one quarter of the substantive core.
